Nobody's talking about the helium problem.

About a third of the world's helium supply which is critical to high-end chip manufacturing, is locked in Qatar.

Iranian strikes have hit Qatari natural gas facilities, which is where helium production comes from and even undamaged supply can't ship because the Strait of Hormuz is closed.

Now the workaround is a pipeline through Saudi Arabia to the Suez Canal, BUT Iran's allies in Yemen have already flagged they're willing to shut that route down too

Trump announced a five-day pause on strikes against Iranian energy infrastructure and claimed the US is in talks with Iran for a "complete resolution." 

BUT Iran flatly denied any talks are happening and said Trump backed down after receiving intelligence that Iran was prepared to hit every power plant in the Middle East.

Meanwhile, crude oil briefly dropped to $85 on the headline. Gas nationally is approaching $4, with California around $6.
